arms.better: tm found the relevant Path implementation and typing examples, but its progress messages repeatedly said only ‘Read src/click/types.py’, including repeated reads and overlapping ranges, so a user could not tell what new information each read added. The first and retry sessions both ended with ‘model ended turn without submitting’; retry repeated the investigation, made no code change, and did not run tests. The suggested `tm run T-1` retry was syntactically clear but failed the same way, while `tm stats --json` showed 511 seconds and 1,386,134 input tokens. A concise planned investigation, deduplicated context across retry sessions, and a terminal summary separating no submission from verification status would make the run clearer and materially cheaper.

OpenCode quickly identified the typing surface, stated a scoped plan, implemented a generic Path type, and recovered cleanly when an added default-type assertion failed by correcting the expected annotation. It reported its verification accurately. It could improve by checking the complete merged typing test rather than adding and iterating on a separate default assertion, and by carrying the issue’s full regression cases through verification before summarizing.
